heroHeadline: 'Operation Epic Fury' Ended (Day 67): US Pauses Project Freedom as Pakistan-Led Iran Diplomacy Advances 'Hormuz First, Nuclear Later' Framework
heroSubtitle: In a dramatic de-escalation on May 5–6, 2026, President Trump paused 'Project Freedom' (the Strait of Hormuz naval escort operation) citing 'great progress' on an Iran deal, and 'Operation Epic Fury' — the US-Israel military campaign against Iran — was declared formally ended on Day 67 (May 6). Pakistan-led mediation has gained traction, with the US signaling acceptance of Iran's preferred 'Hormuz first, nuclear later' sequencing: open the strait to commercial shipping before tackling Iran's nuclear program. Iran FM Araghchi traveled to Beijing to brief China, and Iran confirmed 'messages exchanged' via Pakistani back-channels — but no formal response to the US's 14-point proposal has been issued and no treaty signed. The US naval blockade of Iranian ports remains in place, with 41 Iranian tankers (~69M bbls) still blocked. Brent crude eased from $103–106/bbl to ~$99–102/bbl on diplomatic progress, but analysts warn prices could re-spike if talks collapse. Senate released $72B ICE/CBP reconciliation bill text on May 5 (including $1B for White House ballroom security). Kevin Warsh's Senate floor confirmation vote remains set for the week of May 11 — before Jerome Powell exits May 15.
